_strings.@@b4ccfde5f61a: Treaty conformity — AZ conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from AZ income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the AZ return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Arizona's resident return (Form 140) starts from federal adjusted gross income: 2025 Form 140 line 12 is "Federal adjusted gross income (from your federal return)", and the 2025 instructions state "Arizona uses federal adjusted gross income as a starting point to determine Arizona taxable income. Your federal adjusted gross income is your Arizona gross income." Because federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI, it flows through to the AZ return excluded. AZ then applies only specific statutory additions (2025 Form 140 lines 14-18): the small-business-income modification (lines 13-14), non-Arizona municipal interest (line 15), the partnership income adjustment (line 16), total federal depreciation (line 17, reversed via the line 26 recalculated-Arizona-depreciation subtraction), and line 18 "Other Additions to Income" — whose 2025 schedule (Form 140 page 5) enumerates items A through S: A married persons filing separate returns, B Form 141AZ Schedule K-1 fiduciary adjustment, C ordinary-income portion of federally excluded lump-sum distributions, D items previously deducted for Arizona purposes, E/F claim-of-right repayment adjustments (incl. the NOL variant), G agricultural water conservation expenses / S-corporation pass-through addition, H adjusted-basis add-backs for credit property (Forms 338/325/315), I nonqualified 529 withdrawals, J sole-proprietorship loss of an Arizona nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary, K federal NOL carryforward from non-Arizona sources accrued while a nonresident, L federal capital-loss carryforward from non-Arizona sources before Arizona residency, M ADA access expenditures, N pre-1990 child-care-facility amortization/depreciation, O net capital loss from exchanging one kind of legal tender for another, P entity-level income tax payment, Q motion picture production costs, R other adjustments related to tax credits, S other adjustments, T total. NO line on Form 140 or its additions schedule adds back federal tax-treaty-exempt income (unlike California's Schedule CA). Therefore treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by Arizona -> conforms. (The 2025 list is longer than the 2024 A-J list — items K-S were read line-by-line off the fetched 2025 form and none is a treaty add-back.)

Must be either (a) age 65 or older in 2025, or (b) under 65 but receiving SSI Title 16 income from the Social Security Administration (NOT normal Social Security disability). Total household income must be under the limits below. The claim (or an extension request) must be filed by April 15, 2026.

Claimed via the Form 140 page-3 worksheet (line 7C) with box 44C checked, or the increase may be denied. This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Rate unchanged for 2025: Arizona stays at the 2.5% flat rate for all income levels and filing statuses (first effective 2023). What CHANGED is the standard deduction, which rose to the 2025 federal amounts as raised by the federal reconciliation act ("OBBBA"): $15,750 single/MFS, $31,500 MFJ, $23,625 HoH (from $14,600/$29,200/$21,900 in 2024) — do NOT use the pre-OBBBA $15,000/$30,000/$22,500 projections. The lines 38-41 exemption amounts are unchanged. Arizona has NO personal exemption, and the plain dependent exemption was replaced by the Line 49 Dependent Tax Credit ($100 per qualifying dependent under 17, $25 per dependent 17 or over, phased down when federal AGI exceeds $200,000 — $400,000 MFJ — and gone once the excess tops $19,000). It is a CREDIT against tax, not a base reduction, and is NOT modeled by calc.state_tax. Increased Standard Deduction for charitable contributions (Line 44): non-itemizers may add 34% (.34) of the qualified charitable contributions that would have been allowed had they itemized — RAISED for 2025 from 33% (2024) and 31% (2022) — via the Form 140 page-3 worksheet (line 7C). NOT modeled; claim it on Line 44 with box 44C checked, or the increase may be denied. Exemptions on Form 140 lines 38-41 (age 65+ $2,100; blind $1,500; other $2,300; qualifying parent/grandparent $10,000) reduce Arizona AGI on the form — calc.state_tax does not apply them; a 65+/blind filer computes lines 38-41 on the form. A deceased-spouse special rule applies to Line 43: if you and your deceased spouse would have filed jointly for 2025 enter $31,500, if separately enter $15,750. Not modeled: the Line 47 tax from recapture of Form 301 credits (added to the Line 46 tax at Line 48), the Form 140-SBI small-business-income election (lines 13-14 remove SBI from the Form 140 base and tax it on a separate return), and every Arizona credit (lines 49-58).
